Un filtro deja pasar unas frecuencias y: A filter lets some frequencies through and attenuates others. Its response is the transfer function $H(jω) = V_"out"/V_"in"$, a complex number for each frequency. The Bode plot draws its magnitude in decibels, $20 log |H|$, and its phase, both against frequency on a logarithmic scale. This way, the responses of cascaded filters add up and the asymptotic lines can be drawn by hand.
Un RC o un RL tienen una sola frecuencia: An RC or an RL has a single cutoff frequency, where the gain drops 3 dB ($|H| = 1/√2$) and the phase is ∓45°:
Por encima (paso bajo) o por debajo (pas: Above (low-pass) or below (high-pass) $f_c$ the gain changes by 20 dB per decade. An RC low-pass takes its output across the capacitor; an RC high-pass, across the resistor.
El RLC en serie tiene una frecuencia pro: The series RLC has a natural frequency and a quality factor that sets what the response looks like near it:
Con $Q > 1/√2$ los pasos bajo y alto pre: With $Q > 1/√2$ the low-pass and high-pass show a resonance peak; in the band-pass (measured across the resistor) $Q$ gives how narrow the band is, and in the band-stop, how narrow the notch is. The asymptotes change by 40 dB per decade in the low-pass and high-pass, and ±20 dB per decade in the band-pass.
La fase mide cuánto se retrasa cada frec: Phase measures how much each frequency is delayed; group delay, how much a signal made of nearby frequencies is delayed, such as the envelope of a pulse. It is the derivative of the phase:
En un RC paso bajo vale $τ_g = RC/(1 + (: For an RC low-pass it is $τ_g = RC/(1 + (ωRC)²)$: $RC$ at DC and half of that at the cutoff frequency. A second-order filter with high $Q$ delays frequencies near $f_0$ a lot ($τ_g = 2Q/ω_0$ in the low-pass RLC), which distorts pulses.
